title: Technology Sector Update for 06/22/2018: TWTR,BB,BB.TO,QCOM,NXPI,CHL
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT -0.73%
AAPL +0.25%
IBM +0.13%
CSCO +0.22%
GOOG +0.25%
Technology stocks were edging lower Friday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing slightly more than 0.3% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 0.7% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Twitter ( TWTR ) was trimming a portion of its prior declines, roughly halving a nearly 2% slide previously on Friday, after saying it purchased privately held Smyte to help reduce hateful content on the micro-blogging website. Twitter announced the deal on its @TwitterSafety post, saying the San Francisco-based technology company specializes in safety, spam and security issues and will help it address those issues "more quickly and effectively." Financial terms and other details of the acquisition were not disclosed.
In other sector news:
- BlackBerry Limited (BB,BB.TO) retreated Friday, at one point dropping over 10%, after the smartphone manufacturer swung to a GAAP Q1 net loss of $0.11 per share, reversing a $1.23 per share GAAP profit during the year-ago period. Adjusted revenue also fell year-over-year, dropping to $217 million during the three months ended May 31 from $244 million last year but still beating the $209.6 million Street view, while reported revenue fell to $213 million from $235 million during the same quarter last year. Excluding one-time items, Blackberry earned $0.03 per share, improving on a $0.02 per share in net income during the year-ago period and topping the analyst consenus expecting $0.00 per share.
+ Qualcomm ( QCOM ) was rising Friday, turning around a small mid-morning decline, after the specialty chipmaker extended its cash tender offer for all outstanding shares of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) by another week to June 29. Separately, Qualcomm reportedly is one of seven cornerstone investors who provided China's Xiaomi Corp. with $548 million in new funding ahead of a planned $6.1 billion initial public offering on the Hong Kong stock exchange. Other pre-IPO investors include China Mobile ( CHL ), according to Reuters, which was provided with a term sheet for the deal.
